name: Integrated HR, cyber, legal, and EOR response controls

attribution.legal_posture: This is practitioner observation and legal education from a public panel. It provides general guidance; individualized legal advice, adjudication, one-signal DPRK affiliation, sanctions, and disclosure decisions require jurisdiction- and fact-specific analysis.

ttps: Apply behavior- and access-based review consistently without demographic or protected-characteristic profiling
Coordinate HR, security, legal, compliance, and business stakeholders under a documented incident-response process
Define employer-of-record screening, escalation, evidence-access, and sanctions-compliance responsibilities contractually
Preserve and correlate recruiting, endpoint, network, cloud, access, code, and historical evidence
caveats: Panelists report co-employment, cooperation, severance, and laptop-return observations as contextual possibilities; an individual case needs corroboration.

Nationality, ethnicity, accent, language, age, sex, disability, appearance, and other demographic or protected characteristics are contextual traits; risk decisions require evidence from cited records.
Legal, sanctions, export-control, employment, privacy, monitoring, preservation, and disclosure decisions require qualified counsel and jurisdiction-specific analysis.

Monitoring and investigation controls should be necessary, proportionate, transparent where required, role-based, consistently applied, and focused on job-relevant conduct and authorized-system evidence.
Defensive and response guidance offers guidance only; actor, victim, incident, worker, persona, and legal-identity status are unassigned.

infrastructure.claim: Correlate endpoint, cloud, access, code, and historical records, preserving sufficient evidence to review access outside assigned duties and relevant remote-access or peripheral activity.
Correlate recruiting and HR records with endpoint and network evidence; job-search activity from an employer-managed system may be relevant to a possible co-employment inquiry.
Employer-of-record contracts and procedures should explicitly allocate sanctions-screening, vetting, evidence-access, and escalation responsibilities.

Panelists report that some suspected workers may remain cooperative while seeking another paycheck or severance and may arrange laptop return; this is a practitioner observation, not a prediction about any individual.
Prepare a fact-specific response process covering sanctions, export controls, contracts, regulatory duties, and potential voluntary disclosures rather than assuming a uniform legal outcome.

sources.support: Practitioner panel support for cross-functional investigation, containment, evidence preservation, sanctions-response planning, and explicit allocation of employer-of-record screening responsibilities. These are source-attributed practitioner observations and legal education, not individualized legal advice or proof that a single signal establishes affiliation
